title: Weekend Update- Andrew Dismukes on Great-Grandmas
text: This week, a great-grandmother of three received a college degree from Samford University at the age of 78. Here to talk about his great-grandmother is Andrew Dismukes. Hey! How you doing? I'm good, Andrew. How you been? I've been good. This pandemic's been crazy, huh? Yeah. Yeah, no, I was just saying that to someone the other day. Yeah, of course. So tell us about your great-grandmother. Well, a little bit of context for anyone who hasn't read my photo-less Wikipedia page. I'm from Texas. Great. Got to play the crowd. And, look, I don't ever want to seem like I'm bashing on the place that I'm from or how I was brought up because I'm a proud Texan, you know? I'm Texas through and through. I love Texas barbecue. I love Willie Nelson. And well into my adulthood, I thought that Frazier was British. I was telling everyone, I knew confidently that Frazier was British. And then one day, someone was like, actually, no, he's just fancy. Blew my mind. Anyway, I feel like Texas gets ragged on a lot just because of, like, what it does and the laws it passes and the way its people are, which isn't fair. But I'm very grateful to everyone down there who helped raise me, including my great-grandmother. Oh, cool. Well, I'm glad we finally arrived at the topic. But you came out in disgust. That's great, man. Yeah, well, you know, I wanted to do my Frazier joke. Yeah, I know. Which crushed. Good call, Andrew. Anyway, I was lucky enough to get to grow up most of my childhood while my great-grandmother was still alive. And getting to know her was really cool. Her name was Old Mama. That's what we called her to her face. Much to her protest. I guess we thought that Mama on its own would not properly convey how old this woman was. But every now and then, you'd have to go, like, sit with Old Mama. And it wasn't my favorite thing to do, but I do have one good memory from sitting with Old Mama. She had cable. I cannot believe people here have seen Brink. Yeah, Brink Nation is here tonight. You're a fan of Brink? Oh, love it. Love Brink. I definitely know what it is. Love it. Hell yeah. Boy, uh... Well, for those of you who don't know, Brink is a movie about inline rollerblading gangs who battle it out. And I watched that movie with a woman who was born in the 1800s. It made zero sense to her. She was like, what is a Disney Channel original movie? I was like, I don't know. Usually, it just means it's, like, bad. Usually, they're just not that great, and they're all about how, like, ah, middle school's tough, but also, I'm a mummy. You know? That's what they're all about. Wow.
